1: You spend twenty minutes choosing what to watch.
3: Five apps. Ten thousand titles. Zero decisions.
Not a content problem. (beat) A choosing problem.
4: This is FireDrift. Two ways to pick tonight's movie on Fire TV:
a feed you drive with the remote… and an AI butler you talk to.
5: One title, full screen. Right: like. Left: skip.
Every press teaches it your taste. No login.
6: Found it? Press OK. Watch now opens the app that has it, on your services.
7: Built for the TV: one cover in memory, the D-pad on every screen, running on Vega OS.
(beat) But the feed is the easy part.
8: Still can't decide? Meet your butler.
9: B: He picks one title, tells you why, and the chips change with every answer.
10: Ask for "something lighter"… and he changes your taste. Live.
With an Undo button. You stay in control.
11: He listens. He thinks. He speaks.
And every gesture lands on the exact word.
12: Under the hood: a Strands agent on Bedrock AgentCore, running Claude Haiku.
Transcribe hears you. Polly speaks, and its speech marks drive the animation.
AgentCore Gateway turns our Lambdas into tools.
13: The model never invents a title: TMDB confirms every pick.
And the feed never calls an LLM. Fast, and cheap.
14: FireDrift. Built for the Amazon Developer Hackathon. Open source, on Fire TV.
